llm.summary: This skill is a local Chinese note-and-file organizer that stores user-added content in the browser and does not show hidden network or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: It uses browser clipboard, file picker, drag-and-drop, localStorage, and IndexedDB for user-provided notes, images, and files, which is proportionate to the tool's purpose and is disclosed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill ships as markdown plus a static HTML asset with no install hooks or dependency installation; the packaging command is optional distribution guidance.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation wording is somewhat broad, but it remains tied to note collection, clipboard organization, local archiving, and Word export rather than unrelated agent authority.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Content persists in browser localStorage and IndexedDB until cleared, with user-facing delete/trash controls; there is no evidence of background workers, privilege escalation, credential access, or network upload.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is a single-file local HTML app for collecting text, images, files, organizing them, and exporting Word documents; the inspected HTML implements those same features.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want a Chinese-language, browser-local note and file organizer. Treat saved notes, images, and documents as persistent data in that browser profile, and clear the app storage or trash when handling sensitive material on a shared device.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger examples are broad, but they describe the same local note-taking and document-export workflow implemented by the artifact, so this is a scoping note rather than a security concern.
[SQP-3] expected: The HTML and documentation are intentionally Chinese-language; this may affect usability for non-Chinese users but does not indicate hidden or unsafe behavior.
